pillar_reactions.evidence: Arrived pre-sold on the method and tied it to his own framework unprompted: 'the prospect of learning a completely full skill... how I could have a whole new skill set or mastery, which was that fourth stage in the four stages'. He had already trialled it — 'I tried a kettlebell workout, just one from his videos, and I was like, dude, I did 20 pounds, and I was like sweating hard' — and volunteered why Trevor specifically: 'he really embodies what he teaches... there's that level of integrity'. When the rep described the six-month mastery arc he completed the sentence himself: 'That's the mastery part in four stages, yeah.'

Understood immediately, being a carb cycler already, and asked to pin down the mechanism: 'So is it intermittent fasting in the eight hour window?' Then supplied his own history with it — 'Yeah, I did it. I don't think I did it the best... I don't think during that time I was eating the right nutrition during the eating window' — and closed with 'No, that makes sense.' No resistance, but he was checking specifics rather than simply accepting.

This was the pillar that sold him, and he said so in his own words rather than in the rep's: 'to receive guidance, accountability and support from someone, I feel like it's the right time for that.' He set it against being a therapist — 'I'm a therapist for other people. So I love to be able to receive the feedback, the support, the accountability... I've been the one supporting people.' On the mechanics: 'It seems just like he's going to be very dialed in to my personal lifestyle, and he's going to really modify the program for the lifestyle that I have. That sounds great.'

anchors.raw: the last time I did like personal training was like when I switched back from like yoga calisthenics into weightlifting. And I think he was a personal trainer at the gym, but, and I was, even there, I was like, man, I know more than this guy. I've been probably training more than this guy
anchors.note: His only reference point for paid coaching is a trainer he out-knew. That is a live risk against a $6,000 one-to-one product and the rep did address it indirectly — 'is it going to be Trevor that's going to be coaching me, or someone else?... No, here, that's only Trevor' — which is the right answer, but it arrived by luck rather than because the anchor had been surfaced and worked.

anchors.raw: I'm very independent. That's why I was like, you know, like, you give me a program and I'll do it... I'm used to just give me the program and I'll, I'm going to make it work.
anchors.note: Twenty years of successfully self-directing across yoga, calisthenics, movement school and weightlifting. He can build his own programme and knows it, so the purchase has to be justified by coaching quality rather than programming. He resolved this himself — 'being able to receive somebody else's help and support, I know how important that is' — but if the Trevor relationship disappoints, this is the belief he falls back to.

anchors.raw: I just made, like to be honest, I just made another investment in my business, you know, to open up another part of my business
anchors.note: Not a price objection but a timing one, and the reason the entire payment-plan conversation happened. His discretionary capital was already deployed elsewhere in the same period.

anchors.raw: I run my own business already, so I'm, I'm here for it.
anchors.note: Sells professional services himself as a therapist, so the premise that expert guidance is worth paying for needed no argument. He also holds investments over $100k he can access — the constraint was liquidity and card limits on the day, not net worth, and the rep established that correctly before structuring.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that kettlebell training alone will deliver the same hypertrophy stimulus as loaded barbell work — 'can I get that same stimulus of anabolic stimulus from just kettlebells from like the squats'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep answered 'Yeah, but it's different' and switched to his own recovery story. No mechanism, no evidence, no client example. The prospect's whole reason for buying is a body-composition outcome he has never achieved, and the single technical question underneath it was left open.

unmet_demand.want: A defined leanness outcome — visible abdominal definition he has never reached in twenty years of training
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No guarantee was mentioned on this call at all, unlike every other sale in this batch where the 8kg kettlebell-load guarantee was stated. Even where it is given, that guarantee covers load progression, not body composition, so the prospect's actual goal sits outside what the programme underwrites. Nobody defined what leanness result is being promised, over what period, or how it would be measured.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that works around frequent multi-day dance travel where sleep is the first casualty
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep gave a good directional answer — swap the kettlebell session for bodyweight or mobility on heavy dance days — but then asserted 'I think that the benefits are bigger than the downside of cutting down sleep', which waves away the recovery problem rather than solving it, on a programme that positions recovery as central.
